manifest.name: dsh-coding-discipline
manifest.description: Coding-discipline enhancement for DeepSeek Harness: a Coding agent preset and an embedded coding-discipline skill for verify-first edits, minimal diffs, real test runs and evidence-based reports.
manifest.author: JinBeiCN

bundle.text:
# dsh-coding-discipline — bundle patch for DeepSeek Harness.
#
# Inserts two host-level rows:
#   1. coding-discipline-skill — registers the embedded `coding-discipline` skill
#      (index.js) into the profile's skill layer, so agents can discover and load it.
#   2. preset-coding — a `Coding` agent preset derived from the shipped `standard`
#      preset: the same plugin list and tools, with a strengthened persona.
- insert:
    - id: coding-discipline-skill
      name: dsh-coding-discipline

# Agent preset coding: DeepSeek coding-discipline enhancement bundle.
# Derived from the shipped standard preset (presets/standard.patch.yml).
# The plugin list is copied verbatim from standard except for the persona prefix,
# so the tool set is identical to the baseline and A/B results are comparable.
- insert:
    - id: preset-coding
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: coding
        order: 2
        name: Coding
        description: "Coding preset for DeepSeek models: verify-first workflow, minimal diffs, real test runs and evidence-based reporting."
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: |
                You are a coding agent powered by the {{model}} model.

                Follow this contract for every coding task. It is binding, not advice.

                1. Load the `coding-discipline` skill with the skill tool before planning or editing (when available); its procedure is binding.
                2. Implement and verify from the repository's own task spec, tests and code only. Do not speculate about hidden tests, graders, benchmarks or scoring rules, do not spend reasoning on what they might check, and do not read or list parent/sibling directories, other checkouts, git history or paths outside the working directory for hints. Verification = the repository's own checks against the spec.
                3. Read the task, acceptance criteria and relevant tests/code first. Reproduce the failure with a real command and name the root cause as file:line before your first edit.
                4. Make the smallest change. Do not refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code; preserve public interfaces and existing style.
                5. Never edit, delete, weaken, skip or xfail tests to make code pass, and never hardcode expected values. Tests are the contract.
                6. Verify every API, import and parameter exists in this repository or its installed dependencies before using it. Never invent symbols.
                7. Run the repository's real test/verification command after your last edit and iterate until it passes. "Should pass" is not verification.
                8. If the task has more than ~15 numbered acceptance clauses, keep a clause -> implementation -> verification checklist and tick each off; skip this for normal tasks.
                9. For performance/concurrency tasks, report the quantitative evidence you actually measured once (duration, input size, thread count, retries); no extra stress loops or benchmark reruns.
                10. Report evidence: files changed, root cause, exact commands and observed results, and anything unverified. Never fabricate output. If blocked, report the blocker and what you tried.
                11. Stay in scope and manage long tasks: keep a constraint/todo list, re-read the task before reporting, and if the same approach fails twice, change approach instead of repeating it.
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
          - id: time-context
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context'
          - id: tool-bash
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
            disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
          - id: tool-pwsh
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
            disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
          - id: tool-fs-search
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
            config:
              sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
          - id: tool-jobs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
          - id: tool-schedule
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-schedule'
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: command-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-goal'
          - id: tool-goal
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
          - id: planning
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              planMode: true
            config:
              - id: plan-mode
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
                config:
                  section: |
                    You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until the user approves your plan through exit_plan_mode or switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.

                    Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.

                    The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.

                    Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.

                    Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.

                    When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
              toolResultPruner: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
              - id: tool-result-pruner
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
                config:
                  thresholdChars: 8192
                  headChars: 4096
                  tailChars: 1024
          - id: delegation
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              workflowEngine: true
            config:
              - id: tool-subagent-control
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
              - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'
              - id: tool-subagent
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
                  toolName: subagent
                  modelSelectionSettings: true
              - id: tool-subagent-fork
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
                config:
                  provider: fork
                  toolName: subagent_fork
              - id: workflow-ptc
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'
                config:
                  provider: spawn
              - id: tool-workflow
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'
          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'
          - id: tool-plugin-manager
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager/tools'
            disabled: true
          - id: tool-plugin-market
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market/tools'
            disabled: true

readme.text:
Coding-discipline enhancement for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).

This plugin ships two pieces that work together:

1. **A `Coding` agent preset** (`id: coding`) — the shipped `standard` preset's plugin list with the **same tools**
   and a strengthened persona: verify-first edits, minimal diffs, real test runs, no test gaming, spec-only
   verification, and evidence-based reports. No new tools, no permission changes, so it is comparable with the
   baseline and safe to switch back.
2. **An embedded `coding-discipline` skill** — the full procedure behind the preset contract, registered at host
   level so any agent in the profile can discover and load it on demand. Project/user skills with the same name
   still win by rank.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-coding-discipline
```

From GitHub instead of npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:JinBeiCN/dsh-coding-discipline
```

Install from the release tarball if neither route is available:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/JinBeiCN/dsh-coding-discipline/releases/download/v1.0.0/dsh-coding-discipline-1.0.0.tgz
```

Then use it:

- **New sessions:** choose **Coding** in the agent-preset selector. To make it the default for new sessions,
  set it in Settings → General (Agent preset).
- **Any session:** the `coding-discipline` skill is listed in the skill catalog; load it before coding work.
  Existing sessions are not changed by installing the bundle.

The preset was evaluated against an uninjected baseline on a self-built 16-task coding benchmark with
`deepseek-flash` (`reasoningEffort=max`), 18 isolated agent runs per arm:

So this plugin is a **guardrail**, not a capability booster: it changes how work is done and reported, and it
matters most for weaker models, lower reasoning effort, long specs, or review-heavy delivery. It does not make an
already-saturated model produce more correct code in our benchmark.

- `dsh` `>=0.2.1-rc.2`, Node.js `>=18`.
- Web and Desktop profiles with the agent-preset registry (the shipped `standard` preset must be present, which
  it is in the default `web` profile). Headless/ACP profiles have no preset registry and do not load the preset
  part; the embedded skill part is registered wherever the bundle's host row is mounted.

- Persona: 325 words, charged per request only in sessions that select the `Coding` preset.
- Embedded skill: 7,600 characters of body (7,923 including frontmatter), below the standard preset's
  8,000-character skill budget; it is only charged when a session loads the skill.
- No tools are added or removed.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-coding-discipline
```

Disabling the bundle (or removing it) leaves existing sessions untouched until they are re-created.

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import('./index.js').then(m => console.log(m.name, m.inject))"
```

`index.js` exports a plain Cordis plugin (`name`, `inject`, `apply`) that registers the skill from
`skills/coding-discipline/SKILL.md`; `cordis.patch.yml` inserts that host row plus the `Coding` preset.
No build step and no runtime dependencies.
